subject: biology
title: Neurobiology (HL) Adventure 3: Innate behaviour, learning and perception
welcome_lead: Today you'll explore ethology, learning and the senses.
meta_desc: Biology HL — innate vs learned behaviour, imprinting, conditioning, vision, hearing.
final_note: You learned innate behaviour is inherited, learned modifies it (imprinting, classical/operant conditioning), and senses convert stimuli into APs.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Innate: inherited, no experience needed. E.g. taxis (woodlice move from light), kineses, reflex arcs.

Learned: modified by experience.
- Imprinting (Konrad Lorenz, 1935) — Greylag goslings followed first moving object in critical period.
- Classical conditioning (Pavlov) — bell + food → bell → salivation.
- Operant conditioning (Skinner) — reward shapes behaviour.

Light → cornea → lens (focused) → retina.

Rods — 120 million; one type of rhodopsin; high sensitivity (night vision); no colour.
Cones — 6 million; 3 types (S/M/L) → trichromatic colour vision; concentrated in fovea.

Photoreceptor signals converge: rod-bipolar-ganglion; ganglion fires APs along optic nerve to visual cortex.

Sound waves → outer ear → tympanic membrane → ossicles → oval window → cochlea (fluid).

Hair cells on the basilar membrane bend → APs along auditory nerve.

Different frequencies displace different parts of the membrane (place theory). Range ~20 Hz - 20 kHz, declining with age.
